text:
alex: Hey — after our CI runner upgrade, deploys started failing with 401 invalid_api_key. Same key works locally in curl. Any ideas?
support-bot: Thanks for the report, alex. Can you paste the curl you ran (with key redacted) and the request-id from the response headers if available? Also which runner image are you using? :eyes:
maria: Can you also confirm whether the key is pulled from the env or file? CI runners sometimes add color codes when printing secrets.
alex: Key is injected into a file via the runner helper and then exported: ```export REDWOOD_KEY=$(cat /tmp/secretfile); curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/models``` Response: ```{"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"API key is invalid or expired"}``` No x-request-id in headers, body only. Runner image: company/ci:2026-02-14.
maria: Could be ANSI escape sequences or other non-printables. Try `cat -v /tmp/secretfile` and `xxd -g 1 /tmp/secretfile | head` — that'll show hidden bytes. Also run `echo "$REDWOOD_KEY" | od -An -t x1` to inspect.
alex: Ran `cat -v /tmp/secretfile` and got: ```^[ [32msk-abc123...^[ [0m``` (I think color codes show up like `^[`), and `xxd` showed bytes `1b 5b 33 32 6d` before the key and `1b 5b 30 6d` after.
infra-eng: Yep that's an ANSI CSI sequence (ESC [32m ... ESC [0m) wrapped around the token. When the Authorization header includes those bytes the server rejects it. This often happens if some command wrote the value with colorized output or an echo wrapper.
maria: Quick repro steps to confirm on your side: 1) `printf "%s" "$(cat /tmp/secretfile)" | xxd -p | sed -n '1p'` 2) `curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -H "Authorization: Bearer $(cat /tmp/secretfile)" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/models` You should see 401. Then run `sed -E 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*[a-zA-Z]//g' /tmp/secretfile > /tmp/secret-sanitized` and retry with sanitized file.
alex: Sanitizing removed the escape sequences and deploy succeeded. Thanks.
support-bot: Suggestion: in CI pipeline, set helper to disable colors (e.g., `GITLAB_CI_NO_COLOR=1` or pass `--no-color` to whatever prints the secret). Also consider validating token format before using: length/prefix `sk-` and base64 or hex checks, or run `tr -d '\r\n' | sed -n '1p'` to strip stray newlines.
maria: I'll add a support KB note: "CI runners may inject ANSI color codes into secret files leading to 401 invalid_api_key" with repro commands and fixes. Alex — can you paste the runner job name so we can update the infra docs?
alex: job name `deploy:staging`. Thanks all, closing the thread. :white_check_mark:
